se_tax_social_security_rate.label: Self-employment tax: Social Security (OASDI) portion
se_tax_social_security_rate.note: 12.4% = 6.2% employee + 6.2% employer equivalent. Applies only up to the Social Security wage base (reduced by any W-2 Social Security wages). Also stated on IRS Topic 554 (https://www.irs.gov/taxtopics/tc554).

se_tax_medicare_rate.label: Self-employment tax: Medicare (HI) portion
se_tax_medicare_rate.note: 2.9% = 1.45% x 2. No earnings cap. Additional Medicare Tax (0.9%) is separate (see additional_medicare_tax_rate).

se_tax_total_rate.label: Self-employment tax combined rate below the wage base
se_tax_total_rate.note: 12.4% + 2.9%. Above the wage base only 2.9% (+0.9% Additional Medicare Tax above the filing-status threshold) applies.

se_net_earnings_factor.label: Share of net self-employment profit subject to SE tax
se_net_earnings_factor.note: Net earnings from self-employment = 92.35% of net profit (Schedule C line 31). Computed on Schedule SE.

se_tax_minimum_net_earnings.label: Net earnings from self-employment at or above which SE tax is owed
se_tax_minimum_net_earnings.note: Statutory, not indexed. Church employee income has a separate $108.28 rule (not relevant here). Income tax filing may still be required below this amount.

se_tax_deduction_share.label: Share of SE tax deductible above the line (employer-equivalent portion)
se_tax_deduction_share.note: Deducted on Schedule 1 (Form 1040) in computing AGI. Reduces income tax only, not SE tax itself (the 92.35% factor already accounts for it).

social_security_wage_base_2026.label: 2026 Social Security contribution and benefit base (taxable maximum)
social_security_wage_base_2026.source_title: SSA Office of the Chief Actuary - Contribution and Benefit Base
social_security_wage_base_2026.note: Up from $176,100 in 2025. Announced 2025-10-24 (press release https://www.ssa.gov/news/en/press/releases/2025-10-24.html). Confirmed by SSA 2026 COLA fact sheet.

social_security_wage_base_2027.label: 2027 Social Security contribution and benefit base (taxable maximum)
social_security_wage_base_2027.note: Announced 2026-10-14 with the 3.6% COLA for 2027 (https://www.ssa.gov/blog/en/posts/2026-10-14.html). For tax year 2027, not 2026. Max OASDI SE tax 2027 = 0.124 x 192,300 = $23,845.20.

se_tax_social_security_max_2026.label: Maximum Social Security portion of SE tax in 2026 (derived)
se_tax_social_security_max_2026.source_title: SSA Office of the Chief Actuary - Contribution and Benefit Base

additional_medicare_tax_rate.label: Additional Medicare Tax on wages + SE income above threshold
additional_medicare_tax_rate.note: Applies to combined Medicare wages and SE income above the filing-status threshold; wages are applied against the threshold first. SE losses are not netted. Not deductible as part of the half-SE-tax deduction.

additional_medicare_tax_thresholds.label: Additional Medicare Tax thresholds by filing status
additional_medicare_tax_thresholds.note: Statutory amounts, NOT indexed for inflation.

federal_brackets_single.label: 2026 federal income tax brackets - single (taxable income)
federal_brackets_single.note: Read 'from' as 'over' and 'to' as 'not over'. Rates made permanent by OBBBA (P.L. 119-21, sec. 70101). Also in IRS release IR-2025-103 (2025-10-09). Tax at top of 35% band: $192,979.25.

federal_brackets_married_filing_jointly.label: 2026 federal income tax brackets - married filing jointly
federal_brackets_married_filing_jointly.note: Also applies to qualifying surviving spouse. Consistent across IRS release IR-2025-103 and secondary tables (Capital Group, NerdWallet, Tax Foundation).

federal_brackets_head_of_household.label: 2026 federal income tax brackets - head of household
federal_brackets_head_of_household.note: 24%/32% boundary is $201,750 per the Rev. Proc. table (cumulative tax $16,155 + 24% over $105,700; tax at $640,600 = $191,171, which only reconciles with $201,750). Some secondary sites (incl. Tax Foundation table) show $201,775, which is the single-filer figure.

standard_deduction_2026.label: 2026 standard deduction by filing status
standard_deduction_2026.note: OBBBA made the TCJA-level standard deduction permanent and raised the 2025 amounts to $15,750 / $31,500 / $23,625 (single / MFJ / HOH); 2026 amounts are those indexed for inflation. Additional amounts for age 65+/blind and the temporary OBBBA senior deduction are not included here.

qbi_deduction_rate.label: Qualified Business Income (Section 199A) deduction rate
qbi_deduction_rate.source_title: IRS - One, Big, Beautiful Bill provisions (Working Families Tax Cuts) - individuals and workers
qbi_deduction_rate.note: OBBBA sec. 70105 made Sec. 199A permanent (no more 2025-12-31 sunset) and kept the rate at 20% (the House draft's 23% was not enacted). Deduction also capped at 20% of taxable income minus net capital gain. Taken below AGI; does not reduce SE tax.

qbi_threshold_2026.label: 2026 Sec. 199A threshold (taxable income before QBI deduction) where limitations start
qbi_threshold_2026.note: Below the threshold, the full 20% applies even to a specified service trade or business (SSTB: consulting, law, accounting, health, performing arts, financial services, etc.). MFS figure ($201,775) differs from single due to rounding, as reported by Spidell (https://spidell.com/?p=641291).

qbi_phase_in_range_2026.label: Width of the Sec. 199A phase-in range (OBBBA, from 2026)
qbi_phase_in_range_2026.source_title: IRS - One, Big, Beautiful Bill provisions (Working Families Tax Cuts) - individuals and workers
qbi_phase_in_range_2026.note: Widened from $50,000 / $100,000 (pre-2026) to $75,000 / $150,000 for tax years beginning after 2025. Within the range, the SSTB exclusion and W-2 wage/UBIA limits phase in.

qbi_phase_in_end_2026.label: 2026 taxable income above which SSTB income gets no QBI deduction / W-2 wage limits fully apply
qbi_phase_in_end_2026.note: Threshold + phase-in width. Figures reported from Rev. Proc. 2025-32 by Spidell and Clark.com.

qbi_minimum_deduction.label: OBBBA minimum QBI deduction for active qualified businesses
qbi_minimum_deduction.source_title: IRS - One, Big, Beautiful Bill provisions (Working Families Tax Cuts) - individuals and workers
qbi_minimum_deduction.note: New IRC 199A(i): taxpayers who materially participate in an active qualified trade or business with at least $1,000 of aggregate QBI get a deduction of at least $400. Effective for tax years beginning after 2025; both amounts indexed from 2027. Details confirmed only through secondary sources (law firms, beancount.io) in this session.

qbi_w2_wage_limit.label: QBI deduction above the threshold: limited to 50% of W-2 wages paid by the business (or 25% of W-2 wages plus 2.5% of qualified property); reasonable compensation from an S corporation is not QBI
qbi_w2_wage_limit.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts. In the phase-in range the limit applies proportionally; for a specified service trade or business (SSTB) the applicable percentage reduces QBI and W-2 wages. The site ignores qualified property (UBIA) and uses the 50% wage limit only.

estimated_tax_due_dates_2026.label: Form 1040-ES installment due dates for tax year 2026
estimated_tax_due_dates_2026.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals
estimated_tax_due_dates_2026.note: Periods covered: Jan 1-Mar 31, Apr 1-May 31, Jun 1-Aug 31, Sep 1-Dec 31 (unequal). None of these dates falls on a weekend or legal holiday. Calendar-year individuals only; fiscal-year filers use the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th months and 1st month of the next fiscal year.

estimated_tax_q4_skip_rule.value: The January 15, 2027 installment is not required if the 2026 return is filed by 2027-02-01 and all tax due is paid with it.
estimated_tax_q4_skip_rule.label: Exception to the 4th installment
estimated_tax_q4_skip_rule.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals
estimated_tax_q4_skip_rule.note: February 1, 2027 because January 31, 2027 is a Sunday.

estimated_tax_threshold.label: Expected tax owed (after withholding and refundable credits) from which estimated payments are generally required
estimated_tax_threshold.note: Also stated on the 2026 Form 1040-ES. Payments are required if tax owed >= $1,000 AND withholding/credits are below the safe-harbor amount.

estimated_tax_safe_harbor_current_year_r.label: Safe harbor: share of current-year (2026) tax to prepay
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_current_year_r.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_current_year_r.note: Required annual payment = the smaller of 90% of 2026 tax or 100%/110% of 2025 tax. Farmers/fishermen: 66 2/3%.

estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.label: Safe harbor: share of prior-year (2025) tax to prepay
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.note: Prior-year return must cover a full 12-month year. Replaced by 110% when 2025 AGI exceeds the high-AGI threshold.

estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.label: Safe harbor: share of prior-year tax when prior-year AGI is above threshold
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals
estimated_tax_safe_harbor_prior_year_rat.note: Applies if 2025 AGI > $150,000 ($75,000 if married filing separately for 2026).

estimated_tax_high_agi_threshold.label: Prior-year AGI above which the 110% prior-year safe harbor applies
estimated_tax_high_agi_threshold.source_title: IRS - 2026 Form 1040-ES, Estimated Tax for Individuals

form_1040_due_date_tax_year_2026.label: Due date of the 2026 individual return (Form 1040 with Schedule C and SE)
form_1040_due_date_tax_year_2026.note: Statutory rule: 15th day of the 4th month after year end; 2027-04-15 is a Thursday. The 2027 edition of Pub. 509 (calendar for 2027) was not checked in this session. Extension (Form 4868) moves filing, not payment, to 2027-10-15 (Friday).

form_1099_nec_threshold_2026.label: Form 1099-NEC / 1099-MISC reporting threshold for payments made in 2026 (per payee, per year)
form_1099_nec_threshold_2026.source_title: IRS - Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026)
form_1099_nec_threshold_2026.note: OBBBA (P.L. 119-21) raised the threshold from $600 to $2,000 for payments made after 2025-12-31; same $2,000 applies to backup withholding for these payments. May be adjusted for inflation beginning in calendar year 2027 (2027 amount not yet published). Exceptions reported by secondary sources: royalties stay at $10, gross proceeds paid to attorneys at $600. The payer (client) files, not the freelancer; income is taxable even without a 1099.

form_1099_nec_threshold_2025.label: Form 1099-NEC threshold for payments made in 2025 and earlier

form_1099_nec_due_date_2026_payments.label: Deadline to furnish and file Form 1099-NEC for 2026 payments
form_1099_nec_due_date_2026_payments.source_title: IRS - Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC (Rev. December 2026)
form_1099_nec_due_date_2026_payments.note: Rule: January 31 to both recipient and IRS; January 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so the next business day (Monday 2027-02-01) applies. Derived from the general rule, not read verbatim in the Dec 2026 instructions.

form_1099_k_threshold.label: Form 1099-K threshold for third-party settlement organizations (both conditions must be exceeded)
form_1099_k_threshold.source_title: IRS - IRS issues FAQs on Form 1099-K threshold under the One, Big, Beautiful Bill; dollar limit reverts to $20,000 (IR-2025-107)
form_1099_k_threshold.note: OBBBA retroactively reinstated the pre-ARPA rule (> $20,000 AND > 200 transactions); the $5,000 (2024) / $2,500 (2025) / $600 (2026) phase-in no longer applies. Payment card transactions have no minimum threshold. All income remains taxable whether or not a 1099-K is issued.

backup_withholding_rate.label: Backup withholding rate when a payee fails to provide a correct TIN (Form W-9)
backup_withholding_rate.note: 24% (tied to the 4th-lowest bracket rate, made permanent by OBBBA). Rate confirmed in this session only through secondary sources; not read verbatim on irs.gov.

form_w9_basics.value: Form W-9 (Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification) is completed by the freelancer and given to the client, not to the IRS. It provides legal name, business name/disregarded entity name, federal tax classification (individual/sole proprietor, single-member LLC, S corporation...), address and TIN (SSN or EIN), with a certification that the payee is not subject to backup withholding. A single-member LLC that is a disregarded entity enters the owner's name on line 1 and the owner's TIN. Missing or incorrect TIN can trigger backup withholding.
form_w9_basics.label: Form W-9 basics for freelancers
form_w9_basics.source_title: IRS - About Form W-9, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification
form_w9_basics.note: From Form W-9 instructions (Rev. March 2024) as known; the page was not re-read in this session (irs.gov not reachable, search quota exhausted). Verify current revision.

mileage_rate_business_2026_jan_jun.label: IRS business standard mileage rate per mile, miles driven 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30
mileage_rate_business_2026_jan_jun.source_title: IRS - IR-2025-128: 2026 business standard mileage rate at 72.5 cents per mile
mileage_rate_business_2026_jan_jun.note: Announced 2025-12-29. Depreciation component of the business rate for 2026: 35 cents per mile. Applies to gas, diesel, hybrid and electric vehicles.

mileage_rate_business_2026_jul_dec.label: IRS business standard mileage rate per mile, miles driven 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31
mileage_rate_business_2026_jul_dec.source_title: Thomson Reuters - IRS Announces Midyear Increase in Standard Mileage Rates for Business, Medical, and Moving Expense Purposes
mileage_rate_business_2026_jul_dec.note: Mid-year increase announced by the IRS on 2026-07-13 (Announcement 2026-11, IRB 2026-29, modifying Notice 2026-10) because of fuel prices. Corroborated by SHRM, IFEBP and others, but the irs.gov page itself could not be read. Medical/moving rate 23.5 cents from 2026-07-01; charitable unchanged at 14 cents. A calculator must split 2026 miles by date driven.

home_office_simplified_method.label: Home office deduction - simplified method
home_office_simplified_method.source_title: IRS - Simplified option for home office deduction
home_office_simplified_method.note: Rate unchanged since Rev. Proc. 2013-13 and still on the IRS page. Space must be used regularly and exclusively for business. No depreciation; deduction limited to gross income from the business. Employees cannot claim it (only self-employed). Re-read on 2026-10-23 through search excerpts: the deduction can't exceed the gross income limit and the excess can't be carried over with the simplified method; prior regular-method carryovers can't be used in a simplified-method year. Mortgage interest and real estate taxes stay deductible as itemized deductions (Schedule A). The method is chosen each year.

more_sources.source_title: Publication 587 (2025), Business Use of Your Home - IRS
Topic no. 509, Business use of home - IRS

states_no_individual_income_tax.label: States with no individual income tax on wage/earned income (2026)
states_no_individual_income_tax.source_title: Tax Foundation - 2026 State Income Tax Rates and Brackets
states_no_individual_income_tax.note: Tax Foundation counts 8 states with no individual income tax (AK, FL, NV, NH, SD, TN, TX, WY) plus Washington, which taxes only capital gains (not wages/self-employment income). New Hampshire's interest and dividends tax was repealed from 2025. Business-level taxes can still apply to freelancers (e.g., Washington B&O tax, Tennessee franchise & excise tax on LLCs, Texas franchise tax on LLCs, Nevada commerce tax) - not verified in this session. Local income taxes (e.g., NYC, some Ohio/Pennsylvania cities) are separate.

states_tax_services_by_default.label: States whose sales/gross receipts tax applies to services by default
states_tax_services_by_default.source_title: TaxJar - When should a business charge sales tax on services?
states_tax_services_by_default.note: Secondary source. Hawaii (general excise tax) and New Mexico (gross receipts tax) are gross receipts taxes. In the other states, most professional services (consulting, design, writing, legal, accounting) are not subject to sales tax, but each state lists specific taxable services. Always check the state revenue department. Tax Foundation sales tax breadth data (cited in a Wyoming legislature briefing) ranks HI, NM, SD as broadest bases.

sales_tax_services_washington.value: Since 2025-10-01 (ESSB 5814), Washington retail sales tax applies to newly listed services, including information technology services (help desk, network support, IT consulting, training), certain advertising services, security and others. Professional services delivered electronically are generally not covered per DOR interim guidance. Penalty relief for periods 2025-10-01 to 2026-12-31.
sales_tax_services_washington.label: Washington: sales tax extended to IT, advertising and other services
sales_tax_services_washington.source_title: Washington Department of Revenue - Services newly subject to retail sales tax
sales_tax_services_washington.note: New exclusions took effect 2026-07-01; litigation pending. A 2026 bill (reported as ESSB 6346) may repeal most of the expansion from 2029 - status not confirmed.

sales_tax_services_maryland_it_rate.label: Maryland sales and use tax on data / information technology and software publishing services
sales_tax_services_maryland_it_rate.source_title: Maryland Comptroller - Technical Bulletin No. 56, Sales and Use Tax on Data or Information Technology Services
sales_tax_services_maryland_it_rate.note: Effective 2025-07-01 (Chapter 604, Acts of 2025). Covers services described in NAICS 518, 519, 5415 (computer systems design and related services) and 5132 (software publishing), regardless of the vendor's own NAICS code. Relevant to freelance developers/IT consultants selling to Maryland customers.

value.name: NYC Freelance Isn't Free Act (Local Law 140 of 2016)
value.aggregation: $800 alone or aggregated with contracts with the same hiring party over the prior 120 days
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, no later than 30 days after completion of the work
value.remedies: Double damages for late/unpaid amounts, retaliation damages, attorney's fees; statutory damages for missing contract
value.enforcer: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP), Office of Labor Policy & Standards

freelance_law_nyc.label: New York City freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_nyc.note: Contract must state the work, the pay and the payment date. Hiring party must answer a DCWP complaint within 20 days.

value.name: New York State Freelance Isn't Free Act (General Business Law Article 44-A)
value.aggregation: $800 alone or aggregated with contracts between the same parties over the prior 120 days
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, no later than 30 days after completion of the services
value.remedies: Double damages for late payment, statutory damages for missing contract, attorney's fees; civil penalties for patterns
value.enforcer: New York State Attorney General (after chapter amendment S8039)
value.excluded: Lawyers, licensed medical professionals, construction contractors, certain sales representatives

freelance_law_new_york_state.label: New York State freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_new_york_state.source_title: NYS Department of Labor - Freelance Isn't Free Act
freelance_law_new_york_state.note: Original version (Labor Law 191-d, enforced by NYSDOL) was set for 2024-05-20; chapter amendment S8039 (https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2023/S8039) moved it to GBL Art. 44-A with AG enforcement, effective 2024-08-28. Hiring party must keep contracts 6 years (secondary source). Penalty amounts not verified on an official page.

value.name: Illinois Freelance Worker Protection Act (820 ILCS 193)
value.aggregation: $500 alone or aggregated with contracts with the same contracting entity over the preceding 120 days
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, no later than 30 days after completion of the services
value.remedies: Statutory damages ($500 for refused written contract), costs and reasonable attorney's fees; suit within 2 years of the due date
value.enforcer: Illinois Department of Labor (complaints) and civil action

freelance_law_illinois.label: Illinois freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_illinois.source_title: Illinois Department of Labor - Freelance Worker Protection Act
freelance_law_illinois.note: Applies to contracts taking effect after 2024-07-01, for work performed in Illinois or for an Illinois-based contracting entity. Excludes construction workers, government contracts, employees. Statute: https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/ILCS/Articles?ActID=4441&ChapterID=68. Hiring party keeps contract 2 years. IDOL provides a model contract.

value.name: California Freelance Worker Protection Act (SB 988, Bus. & Prof. Code 18100 et seq.)
value.aggregation: $250 alone or aggregated with contracts with the same hiring party over the prior 120 days
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, no later than 30 days after completion of the services
value.remedies: Civil action; anti-retaliation; attorney's fees (details not verified)

freelance_law_california_state.label: California statewide freelancer payment protection (professional services)
freelance_law_california_state.note: Applies to contracts entered into or renewed on/after 2025-01-01, single-person independent contractors providing professional services. Hiring party keeps contract 4 years. Confirmed via consistent secondary sources; the code text on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not read.

value.name: City of Los Angeles Freelance Worker Protections Ordinance
value.aggregation: $600 or more in a calendar year with the same hiring entity, counting prior contracts
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if no written contract or no date, no later than 30 days after completion of the work
value.remedies: $250 if a requested written contract was refused; up to twice the unpaid amount for late/partial payment; contract value for other violations
value.enforcer: Office of Wage Standards (Bureau of Contract Administration) or civil action

freelance_law_los_angeles.label: Los Angeles freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_los_angeles.source_title: City of Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards - Freelance Worker Protections Summary
freelance_law_los_angeles.note: Effective date is 2023-07-01 (not 2025). Details corroborated by CalChamber and Fisher Phillips; official summary PDF not read in full. Records kept 4 years.

value.name: Minneapolis Freelance Worker Protections (Wage Theft Ordinance amendment)
value.aggregation: $600 or more in a calendar year, or $200 or more for work within 7 consecutive days, same commercial hiring party
value.payment_deadline: Date (or mechanism to set the date) stated in the written contract; no statutory 30-day default found
value.remedies: Penalty reported at $250 per worker for missing written contract; late/short payment is a violation
value.enforcer: Minneapolis Department of Civil Rights - Labor Standards Enforcement

freelance_law_minneapolis.label: Minneapolis freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_minneapolis.source_title: City of Minneapolis Department of Civil Rights - Freelance Worker Protections FAQ
freelance_law_minneapolis.note: Written contract mandatory for commercial hiring parties only (optional for individuals hiring in a personal capacity). Penalty amount from secondary sources.

value.name: Columbus (OH) wage theft ordinance - freelance worker provisions
value.effective_date: 2023 (amendment adopted May 2023; exact effective date not confirmed)
value.aggregation: $250 alone or over a 120-day period with the same hiring party
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, no later than 30 days after completion of the services

freelance_law_columbus_ohio.label: Columbus, Ohio freelancer payment protection
freelance_law_columbus_ohio.source_title: Epstein Becker Green Workforce Bulletin - Columbus, OH Adds Freelance Worker Protections to Its City Code
freelance_law_columbus_ohio.note: Secondary (law firm) source only; no columbus.gov page found. Contract kept 5 years.

value.name: Seattle Independent Contractor Protections Ordinance
value.aggregation: $600 or more in a calendar year (as recalled; not verified)
value.payment_deadline: Date in the contract; if none, within 30 days after completion (as recalled; not verified)

freelance_law_seattle.label: Seattle independent contractor payment protection
freelance_law_seattle.source_title: City of Seattle - Office of Labor Standards
freelance_law_seattle.note: NOT verified in this session (web search quota exhausted before the check). Do not display without verification.

late_fees_federal_rule.value: No federal law sets or caps late fees on invoices between private businesses. A late fee or interest charge is enforceable only if agreed in the contract or accepted terms, and must respect state usury law and the state's liquidated-damages/penalty doctrine (a fee must be a reasonable estimate of the loss, not a penalty). Freelancer protection laws (NYC, NYS, IL, CA, LA...) add statutory remedies such as double damages for late payment but do not set an interest rate.
late_fees_federal_rule.label: Late fees on invoices: general US rule
late_fees_federal_rule.source_title: NYC DCWP - Protecting Freelance Workers (flyer) [for the double-damages remedy]
late_fees_federal_rule.note: General legal principle summarised; no single official page states it. The federal Prompt Payment Act (31 U.S.C. 3901-3907) only covers payments by federal agencies to contractors (interest penalty if paid after the due date, generally 30 days after a proper invoice) - not verified in this session.

value.rule: If a contract does not stipulate a rate, an obligation bears interest at 10% per year after breach (Civil Code 3289(b)); contractual late charges are assessed under the liquidated damages rule (Civil Code 1671).

late_fee_example_california.label: California: default contract interest after breach
late_fee_example_california.source_title: California Legislative Information - Civil Code section 3289
late_fee_example_california.note: From statute knowledge; not verified online in this session (search quota exhausted). California usury limits (Constitution art. XV) are complex and mostly concern loans/forbearance.

value.rule: Civil usury ceiling of 16% per year (General Obligations Law 5-501 with Banking Law 14-a); criminal usury above 25% (Penal Law 190.40). Whether an invoice late fee counts as interest depends on the case.

late_fee_example_new_york.label: New York: usury ceilings relevant to late interest
late_fee_example_new_york.source_title: NY State Senate - General Obligations Law section 5-501
late_fee_example_new_york.note: From statute knowledge; not verified online in this session. Corporations generally cannot raise civil usury as a defense. Confirm before publishing any cap in a calculator.

retirement_limits_2026.label: 2026 retirement plan limits (401(k) deferral, catch-up, section 415(c), compensation limit, IRA)
retirement_limits_2026.source_title: IRS - COLA increases for dollar limitations on benefits and contributions (Notice 2025-67)

sep_self_employed_rate.label: SEP-IRA and solo 401(k) employer contribution for a self-employed person: 20% of net earnings (net profit minus half of SE tax)
sep_self_employed_rate.source_title: IRS - Publication 560, Retirement Plans for Small Business
sep_self_employed_rate.note: The 25% plan rate becomes 20% for the self-employed because the contribution itself reduces compensation (25% / 125%).

fica_rates_2026.label: FICA on wages (2026): Social Security 6.2% and Medicare 1.45%, each for employer and employee (Social Security wage base: rule social_security_wage_base_2026)
fica_rates_2026.source_title: Topic no. 751, Social Security and Medicare withholding rates - IRS
fica_rates_2026.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of Topic 751 and Publication 15 (2026). No cap on Medicare. Additional Medicare Tax (0.9%, employee only) withheld on wages over $200,000; liability by filing status (rule additional_medicare_tax_thresholds).

futa_2026.label: Federal unemployment tax (FUTA): 6.0% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages, credit up to 5.4% (0.6% net)
futa_2026.source_title: Topic no. 759, Form 940, Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment (FUTA) Tax Return - IRS
futa_2026.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts. The full credit requires state unemployment taxes paid on time and a state that is not a credit reduction state (credit reduction raises the net rate). State unemployment tax itself is not included on the site.

scorp_reasonable_compensation.value: An S corporation must pay a shareholder-employee reasonable compensation for services before making non-wage distributions; the IRS can recharacterize distributions as wages subject to employment taxes. There is no fixed formula: training, duties, time devoted and what comparable businesses pay are among the factors.
scorp_reasonable_compensation.label: S corporation: reasonable compensation of shareholder-employees
scorp_reasonable_compensation.source_title: S corporation compensation and medical insurance issues - IRS
scorp_reasonable_compensation.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts. Payments generated by the shareholder's own services should be wages; income from non-shareholder employees or capital can support distributions. Health insurance premiums paid for a more-than-2% shareholder-employee are reported as wages on the shareholder's W-2 (box 1), not subject to Social Security, Medicare or FUTA when provided under a plan for employees generally.

scorp_income_not_se.value: S corporation income passed through to shareholders (Schedule K-1) is not self-employment income and is not subject to self-employment tax.
scorp_income_not_se.label: S corporation income is not subject to self-employment tax
scorp_income_not_se.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of the Form 1120-S instructions. Form 1120-S is due by the 15th day of the 3rd month after year end (March 16, 2026 for calendar year 2025).

single_member_llc_default.value: A single-member LLC is disregarded as an entity separate from its owner by default: its income and expenses go on the owner's return (Schedule C). It can elect to be taxed as an S corporation by filing Form 2553 (which also counts as the election to be classified as a corporation).
single_member_llc_default.label: Single-member LLC: taxed like a sole proprietorship by default; S corporation by election
single_member_llc_default.source_title: Single member limited liability companies - IRS
single_member_llc_default.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of the IRS page and the Form SS-4 and Form 2553 instructions. A disregarded LLC is still a separate entity for employment and certain excise taxes.

us_sole_prop_default.value: You're automatically considered a sole proprietorship if you do business activities but don't register as any other kind of business; you don't need to register it at the state level.
us_sole_prop_default.label: Sole proprietorship: formed automatically, no state registration
us_sole_prop_default.source_title: Choose a business structure - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_sole_prop_default.note: A sole proprietorship has no legal separation from its owner. Registering a business name (DBA), licenses and tax registrations are separate steps (us_dba, us_licenses, us_state_tax_id).

us_dba.value: Many states require sole proprietors to use their own name for the business unless they file another name, called a DBA (doing business as), trade name, assumed name or fictitious name, with the state or county; a few states don't require it.
us_dba.label: Business name other than your own: DBA registration
us_dba.source_title: Register your business - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_dba.note: Where to file (secretary of state, county clerk) depends on the state and sometimes the county. A DBA doesn't give legal protection of the name by itself.

us_licenses.value: Licenses and permits depend on your business activity and location: federal for some regulated activities, state and local (city or county) for others.
us_licenses.label: Business licenses and permits
us_licenses.source_title: Apply for licenses and permits - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_licenses.note: Requirements vary by state, county and municipality: check your state, city and county websites.

needed_when: you file excise or pension plan tax returns

us_ein.label: EIN for a sole proprietor

more_sources.source_title: Get federal and state tax ID numbers - U.S. Small Business Administration

us_ein.note: A sole proprietor without employees who doesn't file excise or pension plan tax returns doesn't need an EIN (but can get one) and uses their Social Security number as taxpayer identification number. An EIN is needed once you hire an employee or file excise or pension plan returns; banks may ask for one to open some retirement accounts. Applying is free (SBA, IRS online assistant).

us_state_tax_id.value: Whether you need a state tax ID (for example a sales tax permit) depends on whether your business owes state taxes: check with your state's Department of Revenue.
us_state_tax_id.label: State tax registration (state tax ID, sales tax permit)
us_state_tax_id.source_title: Get federal and state tax ID numbers - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_state_tax_id.note: The process varies by state; the SBA's state registration lookup lists the office to contact. Which states tax services: states_tax_services_by_default and the state-specific rules.

us_records_retention.label: How long to keep business tax records (general rule)

more_sources.source_title: Publication 583, Starting a Business and Keeping Records - IRS

us_records_retention.note: Keep records until the period of limitations for the return runs out: generally 3 years from the date you filed (a return filed early counts as filed on the due date). Longer periods: 6 years if you leave out income over 25% of the gross income shown, 7 years for a worthless securities or bad debt deduction, no limit for a fraudulent return or no return; employment tax records at least 4 years; property records until the period of limitations ends for the year you dispose of it (Publication 583).

us_business_bank_account.value: A business bank account keeps business funds separate from personal funds, which matters because a sole proprietorship has no legal separation from its owner; a sole proprietor can use a Social Security number instead of an EIN to open one.
us_business_bank_account.label: Business bank account (recommended)
us_business_bank_account.source_title: Open a business bank account - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_business_bank_account.note: A recommendation, not a legal requirement for a sole proprietor. Banks may ask for a business license or DBA documents.

ssa_benefits_based_on_earnings.value: Social Security benefits are based on your lifetime covered earnings (wages and net self-employment earnings), not on the taxes you paid.
ssa_benefits_based_on_earnings.label: Social Security benefits depend on covered earnings
ssa_benefits_based_on_earnings.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of SSA publications (benefits based on the highest 35 years of indexed earnings). A lower S corp salary therefore means lower earnings on the owner's record.

us_foreign_currency_translation.value: Report every amount in US dollars. Translate a foreign-currency payment at the exchange rate in effect when you receive it (spot rate); income received evenly through the year can be translated at the IRS yearly average rate. The IRS has no official exchange rate and generally accepts any posted rate used consistently.
us_foreign_currency_translation.label: Foreign-currency income: translation into US dollars
us_foreign_currency_translation.source_title: Foreign currency and currency exchange rates - IRS
us_foreign_currency_translation.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts (irs.gov not reachable directly). Yearly averages: https://www.irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/yearly-average-currency-exchange-rates. A self-employed person with a foreign qualified business unit (QBU) can have another functional currency: not covered by the site.

us_form_6166.value: To claim a reduced rate of foreign withholding under a US income tax treaty, a US resident can ask the IRS for Form 6166 (certification of US residency) with Form 8802, then send it to the foreign payer or withholding agent.
us_form_6166.label: Form 6166: US residency certification for treaty benefits
us_form_6166.source_title: Form 6166 - Certification of U.S. tax residency - IRS
us_form_6166.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts. Some countries apply the treaty rate at payment, others withhold the full rate and refund the excess. Form 6166 cannot be used to prove US tax paid for a foreign tax credit. The US-Hungary treaty was terminated from 2024-01-01.

us_ftc_source_rule.value: The foreign tax credit (Form 1116) is limited to the US tax on foreign-source income. Self-employment income is sourced where the work is performed (often apportioned by time): work done in the United States gives US-source income, even for a foreign client, unless a treaty re-sources it.
us_ftc_source_rule.label: Foreign tax credit: source of self-employment income
us_ftc_source_rule.source_title: Publication 514, Foreign Tax Credit for Individuals - IRS
us_ftc_source_rule.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts of Pub. 514 (2025): self-employed taxpayers use the method that most correctly reflects the source, in many cases a time basis; income re-sourced by treaty has its own Form 1116 category. Consequence (site wording): foreign tax withheld on work done in the US is often not creditable; ask the foreign payer to apply the treaty rate first.

us_fbar.label: FBAR (FinCEN Form 114): foreign financial accounts over $10,000 in total at any time in the year
us_fbar.source_title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) - IRS
us_fbar.note: Read on 2026-10-22 through search excerpts. Filed with FinCEN (BSA E-Filing), not with the tax return; automatic extension to October 15; aggregate value of all foreign accounts. Form 8938 (FATCA) has separate, higher thresholds: not covered.

us_small_claims_limits.note: Read through search excerpts of each state's court or legislature pages on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 (details in documentation/24-recouvrement-uk-us-ca.md, § 3). Most limits exclude interest and costs (AK, AZ, CO, DC, FL, HI, IA, IL, KY, LA, MD, ME, MO, NH, OH, PA, RI, VA, WV); TX and UT count attorney fees; CT counts attorney fees and collection costs. CA: $12,500 for natural persons including sole proprietors (CCP 116.221), $6,250 for other parties (CCP 116.220); AB 1827 ($15,000) held in committee 13/08/2026. WA: $10,000 natural persons, $5,000 any other party (RCW 12.40.010). NY: $10,000 in New York City, $5,000 in City Courts, $3,000 in Town and Village Courts; corporations, partnerships and associations file commercial claims up to $10,000 in NYC and $5,000 in City Courts (not in Town and Village Courts). NC: limit set by county from $5,000 to $10,000 (magistrates). PA: $12,000 before magisterial district judges, $10,000 in Philadelphia Municipal Court. GA: $25,000 for actions filed on or after 1 January 2027 (HB 999, Act 707). WI: $15,000 from 1 January 2027 (2025 Act 105); tort and personal injury claims are capped at $5,000 now. ID: $15,000 since 1 July 2026 (S 1330, 2026 ch. 196). ME: $10,000 since 1 January 2026. WV: $20,000 since 7 July 2025 (HB 2761). AZ: $5,000 (SB 1022, Laws 2025 ch. 94). OR: $10,000; SB 484 ($20,000) died in committee in 2025. SC: $7,500; 2025-26 bills to raise it not enacted as of October 2026. TN: $25,000 in general sessions courts under present law (fiscal note of SB 572), other limits in a few larger counties by private act; HB 982 ($50,000) taken off notice on 18/03/2026. MN: $4,000 for consumer credit transactions. VT: $5,000 for consumer credit and medical debt. Representation: IL (corporation needs a lawyer), DC (a business plaintiff needs a lawyer), NJ (a corporation needs a lawyer above $5,000), IN (a corporation without a lawyer only up to $6,000), MI (no lawyers; MCL 600.8408), NE (no lawyers), VA (generally no lawyers), WA (lawyers only with the judge's permission).

us_business_bank_account_irs.value: One of the first things you should do when you start a business is open a business checking account, kept separate from your personal checking account; deposit all receipts in it and reconcile it each month.
us_business_bank_account_irs.label: IRS: open a separate business checking account when you start
us_business_bank_account_irs.source_title: Publication 583 (12/2024), Starting a Business and Keeping Records - IRS
us_business_bank_account_irs.note: Pub. 583 also says to write checks payable to yourself only when withdrawing money from the business for personal use. A recommendation, not a legal requirement.

us_ein_entities.label: EIN: LLCs, partnerships and corporations
us_ein_entities.source_title: Single member limited liability companies - IRS

more_sources.source_title: Instructions for Form SS-4 (12/2025) - IRS

us_ein_entities.note: A single-member LLC with no employees and no excise tax filings doesn't need an EIN, but can get one to open a bank account. A partnership or corporation must use an EIN even without employees; an LLC with two or more members is a partnership by default. Applying is free. Register an LLC, partnership or corporation with the state before applying.

us_llc_separate_funds.value: Keeping business funds separate from personal funds is part of the limited personal liability protection of an LLC or corporation.
us_llc_separate_funds.label: LLC or corporation: keep business funds separate
us_llc_separate_funds.source_title: Open a business bank account - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_llc_separate_funds.note: SBA: a business bank account offers limited personal liability protection by keeping business funds separate from personal funds; banks commonly ask for an EIN (or the owner's Social Security number for a sole proprietorship), formation documents, ownership agreements and a business license. State law decides when a court disregards an LLC's liability protection: not covered here.

us_employer_insurance.label: Insurance required for businesses with employees
us_employer_insurance.source_title: Get business insurance - U.S. Small Business Administration

more_sources.source_title: Hire and manage employees - U.S. Small Business Administration

us_employer_insurance.note: Read through search excerpts. SBA: every business with employees must have workers' compensation, unemployment and disability insurance; in practice these are state rules: workers' compensation under state law (rules and cost vary by state), unemployment insurance tax through the state workforce agency, and disability insurance required only in California, Hawaii, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island and Puerto Rico. Laws requiring insurance vary by state: check your state's website.

us_texas_workers_comp.label: Texas: workers' compensation is optional for most private employers
us_texas_workers_comp.source_title: Workers' compensation: employer information - Texas Department of Insurance

more_sources.source_title: Employer E-File online reporting (non-subscribers) - Texas Department of Insurance

us_texas_workers_comp.note: Read through search excerpts. Texas is the only state where most private employers can choose not to carry workers' compensation. An employer without it posts a notice of no coverage where employees can see it (English, Spanish and other languages as needed), gives written notice to new employees, and files a notice (DWC Form-005) with the Division of Workers' Compensation each year between February 1 and April 30, after hiring its first employee and after ending a policy.

us_workers_comp_owners.label: Workers' compensation for business owners: usually not covered, opt-in depends on the state
us_workers_comp_owners.source_title: Rethinking insurance coverage - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_workers_comp_owners.note: Read through search excerpts of an SBA article. Sole proprietors, partners and LLC members who aren't employees are usually not covered by workers' compensation; state law may allow them to opt in. Businesses in every state must provide it to employees, family members included, with rules and costs that vary by state.

value.commercial_property: businesses with significant property and physical assets

us_business_insurance_types.label: Common types of business insurance (SBA)
us_business_insurance_types.source_title: Get business insurance - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_business_insurance_types.note: Read through search excerpts. General liability: bodily injury, property damage, medical expenses, libel, slander, defending lawsuits and judgments. Professional liability: client claims of mistakes (malpractice), negligence or unfinished work. Home-based business insurance: added to homeowner's insurance as a rider, it can cover a small amount of business equipment and liability for third-party injuries.

single_llc_keeps_owner_ein_unless: it elects to be taxed as a corporation or S corporation
value.single_llc_default_tax_treatment: disregarded entity (reported on the owner's return, Schedule C for an individual)

us_new_ein_rules.source_title: When to get a new EIN - IRS

Entities - IRS frequently asked questions

us_new_ein_rules.note: Read through search excerpts. By default, the IRS treats a single-member domestic LLC as a disregarded entity: its income and expenses go on the owner's return (Schedule C for an individual), unless it elects corporate or S corporation treatment (Instructions for Form SS-4, 12/2025; IRS entity FAQ).

us_s_election_deadline.label: Form 2553: deadline to elect S corporation status
us_s_election_deadline.note: Read through search excerpts. No more than 2 months and 15 days after the beginning of the tax year the election is to take effect, or at any time during the preceding tax year. An eligible entity that files Form 2553 doesn't also file Form 8832. Late election relief for reasonable cause, generally within 3 years and 75 days of the effective date.

us_llc_formation.label: Forming an LLC with your state
us_llc_formation.source_title: Register your business - U.S. Small Business Administration
us_llc_formation.note: Read through search excerpts. Fees vary by state; many states require an annual report or biennial statement, with fees; converting from a sole proprietorship may require new business licenses depending on state and local law.

us_home_office_regular_method.label: Home office deduction - regular method (actual expenses)
us_home_office_regular_method.source_title: Publication 587 (2025), Business Use of Your Home - IRS

more_sources.source_title: Topic no. 509, Business use of home - IRS

us_home_office_regular_method.note: Read through search excerpts. The space must be used regularly and exclusively as the principal place of business or to meet clients (exceptions: storage when the home is the only fixed location, daycare). Indirect home expenses are allocated by the share of floor space; direct expenses are deductible in full. The deduction can't exceed the gross income limitation (figured on Form 8829, which first takes the business part of mortgage interest, taxes and casualty losses, and other business expenses); the excess is carried over to the next year. The tool approximates the limit with the profit before the deduction and doesn't figure depreciation.

value.immunity: An individual shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any Federal or State trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made in confidence to a Federal, State, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney, solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or is made in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal.
value.retaliation_lawsuit: An individual who files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose the trade secret to the attorney of the individual and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, if the individual files any document containing the trade secret under seal and does not disclose the trade secret, except pursuant to court order.
value.without_notice: no exemplary damages or attorney fees against an employee who was not given notice

dtsa_whistleblower_immunity.label: Defend Trade Secrets Act: whistleblower immunity and the notice employers must give

more_sources.source_title: Public Law 114-153, Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016 - Congress.gov

dtsa_whistleblower_immunity.note: § 1833(b)(1) and (2) (immunity and anti-retaliation lawsuits); (b)(3): an employer shall provide notice of the immunity in any contract or agreement with an employee that governs the use of a trade secret or other confidential information (or cross-reference a reporting policy); applies to contracts entered into or updated after May 11, 2016; (b)(4): 'employee' includes any individual performing work as a contractor or consultant for an employer. The immunity does not cover public disclosure. Read through search excerpts.

trade_secret_reasonable_measures.note: A trade secret must be information whose owner has taken reasonable measures to keep it secret (18 U.S.C. § 1839(3)); the USPTO toolkit says reasonableness is judged case by case and lists these measures as examples. Read through search excerpts.

public_holidays.label: Federal holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103), observed dates, 2024 to 2030
public_holidays.source_title: U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM), "Federal Holidays" (holiday schedule for each year)
public_holidays.note: Read in full on 29/10/2026 with the « Lire une source officielle » tool (SHA-256 37973681…2e92). 11 federal holidays a year (5 U.S.C. 6103(a)); the dates are the days OPM lists, i.e. the days observed by most federal employees: a holiday on a Saturday is observed on the preceding Friday (5 U.S.C. 6103(b)), on a Sunday on the following Monday (Executive Order 11582, section 3(a)); substitute = observed on another day than the legal date. Each holiday is stored under the year of its observed date: New Year’s Day 2028 (a Saturday) is observed on Friday 31 December 2027, so 2027 lists 12 days and 2028 lists 10. Inauguration Day (5 U.S.C. 6103(c), Washington, DC, area only, every fourth year) is left out. OPM publishes the schedule up to 2030; add 2031 when it is published. States, local governments and private businesses may observe other days or use other names.
